definitions.explanation: A newspaper that covers news primarily for a specific region or prefecture, as opposed to national newspapers. Japan has many strong regional papers with loyal local readerships.

examples.japanese: そのニュースは{地方紙|ちほうし}にしか{載|の}っていなかった。
examples.english: That news was only in the local newspaper.

examples.japanese: {地方紙|ちほうし}は{地域|ちいき}の{細|こま}かいニュースを{取|と}り{上|あ}げるので、{全国紙|ぜんこくし}にはない{情報|じょうほう}がある。
examples.english: Regional newspapers cover detailed local news, so they contain information not found in national papers.

notes:
A compound of {地方|ちほう} (region, locality) and {紙|し} (paper, short for {新聞|しんぶん}). Japan has a robust regional newspaper tradition, with papers like the {北海道新聞|ほっかいどうしんぶん}, {中日新聞|ちゅうにちしんぶん}, and {西日本新聞|にしにほんしんぶん} having very high readership in their regions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {地方紙|ちほうし}の{記事|きじ} — a regional newspaper article
- {地方紙|ちほうし}の{記者|きしゃ} — a local newspaper reporter
- {県紙|けんし} — prefectural newspaper (more specific)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {全国紙|ぜんこくし} — national newspaper (antonym)
- {新聞|しんぶん} — newspaper (general term)
- {夕刊|ゆうかん} — evening paper
